pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.summary: mem0 is a polyglot monorepo centered on the mem0 Python SDK (PyPI mem0ai) and its TypeScript twin mem0-ts, each exposing two usage modes from one import surface: a self-hosted Memory/AsyncMemory engine and a thin hosted MemoryClient. The self-hosted engine is fully config-driven: a single MemoryConfig Pydantic model drives four factories that lazily instantiate concrete LLM, embedding, vector-store, and reranker providers behind abstract base classes. Each provider category follows a consistent plugin shape (base.py + concrete modules + config + factory registry). Graph memory, formerly a fifth category, has been removed from the OSS core and replaced by in-pipeline entity linking.

surprises.title: Provider counts in AGENTS.md are stale
surprises.detail: AGENTS.md advertises 24 LLMs / 30 vector stores / 15 embeddings / 4 graph stores / 5 rerankers. Counting the actual factory-registered provider modules in the tree (excluding base.py/configs.py/__init__.py/utils.py/mock.py) yields 18 LLMs / 24 vector stores / 11 embeddings / 5 rerankers, and zero graph stores.

surprises.title: Graph memory fully removed from OSS core
surprises.detail: There is no mem0/graphs/ directory, no graph factory in mem0/utils/factory.py, no graph field on MemoryConfig, and grep -in graph mem0/memory/main.py returns nothing. The TS OSS tree (mem0-ts/src/oss/src/) also has no graphs/ dir, contradicting AGENTS.md which still lists src/graphs/. Relationship retrieval is now handled by entity linking inside the vector pipeline.

surprises.title: Factories store providers as dotted strings for lazy import
surprises.detail: Each factory's provider_to_class maps a provider name to a dotted import path (e.g. 'mem0.vector_stores.qdrant.Qdrant') resolved on demand via load_class (importlib.import_module + getattr). Heavy optional backend SDKs are only imported when that provider is selected; unknown names raise ValueError at create() time.

surprises.title: Reranker directory is singular and providers are suffixed
surprises.detail: The reranker category lives in mem0/reranker/ (singular, not rerankers/) and its provider files carry a _reranker suffix (cohere_reranker.py, llm_reranker.py). Reranking is also entirely opt-in: MemoryConfig.reranker defaults to None and self.reranker is only built if configured.

surprises.title: Category __init__.py registries are partial; the factory is the source of truth
surprises.detail: mem0/reranker/__init__.py re-exports only 3 of the 5 factory-supported rerankers and mem0/llms/__init__.py is empty. The authoritative list of supported providers is the factory's provider_to_class dict, not the package init.

surprises.title: EmbedderFactory can return a MockEmbeddings
surprises.detail: When the vector store is upstash_vector with enable_embeddings set, EmbedderFactory.create returns a MockEmbeddings instance so the vector store performs its own embedding rather than the SDK embedder.

pages.title: Data Flow
pages.summary: Traces the two engine hot paths end to end. add() normalizes messages then runs either an infer=False verbatim fast path or the infer=True V3 phased batch pipeline: existing-memory retrieval, one ADD-only LLM extraction call, batch embedding, MD5 hash dedup, batch vector upsert, batch SQLite history insert, batch entity linking, message buffering, and telemetry. search() embeds the query while computing BM25 keyword and entity-store signals, fuses them additively over an adaptive divisor in score_and_rank(), and optionally reranks. AsyncMemory mirrors both paths with asyncio.to_thread around every blocking call (and asyncio.gather only in delete_all); notably there is no temporal ranking at query time — temporal reasoning is an extraction-time concern.

surprises.title: add() extraction is ADD-only — no UPDATE/DELETE on the add path
surprises.detail: The single LLM call in _add_to_vector_store uses ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT and only emits ADD operations with optional linked_memory_ids. Dedup is mechanical (MD5 hash against existing + within-batch) and the LLM is told to skip already-captured facts. UPDATE/DELETE only occur when a caller invokes update()/delete() directly. This is a deliberate departure from the older two-pass fact+decision design.

surprises.title: No temporal/recency ranking in search scoring
surprises.detail: score_and_rank in mem0/utils/scoring.py fuses only semantic + BM25 + entity_boost; it never weights by created_at or recency. Temporal reasoning happens at extraction time — the ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT grounds relative references like 'last week' to concrete dates against the Observation Date before storing. Time-awareness is baked into the stored text, not a query-time signal.

surprises.title: Threshold gates the semantic score BEFORE fusion
surprises.detail: In score_and_rank, any candidate with semantic_score < threshold is dropped before combining, so BM25 or entity boosts cannot rescue a sub-threshold semantic match. The combined score divisor (max_possible) adapts globally per query: 1.0 semantic-only, 1.5 +entity, 2.0 +BM25, 2.5 all three.

surprises.title: Candidate pool is seeded only from semantic results
surprises.detail: _search_vector_store over-fetches max(limit*4, 60) semantic results, then BM25/entity scores only re-rank within that pool. A memory matching BM25 or an entity but absent from the semantic top-internal_limit cannot surface in results.

surprises.title: infer=False skips the LLM, dedup, and entity linking entirely
surprises.detail: The fast path stores each message verbatim via _create_memory: one embed + one vector insert + one ADD history row per message, with name promoted to actor_id. No existing-memory search, no extraction call, no hash dedup against the corpus, no entity linking — minimizing latency and cost for pre-cleaned facts.

surprises.title: AsyncMemory uses to_thread sequentially, not gather, inside add/search
surprises.detail: Both async _add_to_vector_store and _search_vector_store wrap each blocking call in asyncio.to_thread but await them in sequence — the steps are not run concurrently. asyncio.gather appears only in AsyncMemory.delete_all to fan out per-memory deletes. The reranker is dispatched via asyncio.to_thread so it cannot block the event loop.

surprises.title: Entity boosts are spread-attenuated and capped at 0.5
surprises.detail: _compute_entity_boosts weights each match by similarity * ENTITY_BOOST_WEIGHT(0.5) * (1 / (1 + 0.001*(num_linked-1)^2)), so a promiscuous entity linked to many memories contributes a smaller per-memory boost. Only entity-store matches with similarity >= 0.5 count; entity upsert/link uses a stricter >= 0.95 match threshold.

surprises.title: Conversation context is saved even when nothing is extracted
surprises.detail: If the LLM extracts nothing or all extractions are hash duplicates, _add_to_vector_store still calls db.save_messages before returning [], preserving the rolling 10-message buffer for the next turn's Phase-0 context.

pages.title: Memory Engine
pages.summary: The Memory Engine documents the OSS core of mem0: the Memory and AsyncMemory classes in mem0/memory/main.py, both built on the abstract MemoryBase, that orchestrate embedding, vector storage, single-pass LLM extraction, entity linking, and a local SQLite change log. It covers construction (Memory(config) and from_config), every public method's signature and semantics (add/search/get/get_all/update/delete/delete_all/history/reset), the sync-vs-async design where AsyncMemory mirrors Memory via asyncio.to_thread, the SQLiteManager history/messages schema and migration, session scoping with required identifiers, metadata shaping, the infer=False raw path, telemetry, and the ~/.mem0 setup. It surfaces gotchas around required identifiers, filters-vs-top-level kwargs, and async/sync error-type drift.

surprises.title: add() is ADD-only — no LLM-driven UPDATE/DELETE
surprises.detail: The inference path issues exactly one LLM call producing a JSON {"memory":[...]} list of new facts, then dedupes against existing memories purely by md5 hash. Unlike older mem0, the engine no longer asks the LLM to emit UPDATE/DELETE operations during add().

surprises.title: search/get_all reject top-level identifiers but add does not
surprises.detail: _reject_top_level_entity_params raises ValueError if user_id/agent_id/run_id are passed as top-level kwargs to search() or get_all(); they must go inside filters={...}. add() is the exception and accepts them directly. This asymmetry is a common runtime trap.

surprises.title: Async and sync raise different exception types for bad memory_type
surprises.detail: Sync add() raises Mem0ValidationError VALIDATION_002 for an invalid memory_type, but async add() raises a plain ValueError for the identical condition. Catching Mem0ValidationError will miss the async path.

surprises.title: add() returns empty results silently on extraction failure
surprises.detail: If the LLM extraction call fails, returns nothing, or all candidates are hash-deduped, add() logs at error/debug level and returns {"results": []} without raising — it still persists the raw messages. Callers must check the list rather than assume a write occurred.

surprises.title: AsyncMemory is a full duplicate, not a wrapper
surprises.detail: Every method body is copied; async-ness comes solely from wrapping blocking calls (embed, vector ops, LLM, SQLite, lemmatize, entity extraction) in asyncio.to_thread. The only genuine parallelism is delete_all using asyncio.gather. The single shared SQLite connection (check_same_thread=False) is protected by a process-local threading.Lock.

surprises.title: History migration is lossy-by-design
surprises.detail: _migrate_history_table renames the old history table, recreates the new schema, and copies only the intersection of old and new columns inside one transaction — legacy group-chat columns are dropped and new columns left NULL.

surprises.title: Telemetry hashes identifiers and samples hot paths
surprises.detail: process_telemetry_filters md5-hashes user_id/agent_id/run_id into encoded_ids and only reports filter key names. Lifecycle events (init/reset/_create_procedural_memory/$identify) always fire at 100%; hot-path events obey MEM0_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE (default 0.1). MEM0_TELEMETRY=False disables everything. mark_aliased stores an sha256 of anon_id+email, never the plaintext email.

surprises.title: delete_all requires an identifier; there is no wipe shortcut
surprises.detail: delete_all raises ValueError if called with no user_id/agent_id/run_id, explicitly directing callers to use reset() to clear everything.

surprises.title: Qdrant entity store shares the primary client
surprises.detail: For embedded qdrant the lazily-built entity store reuses the primary vector store's client object rather than opening a second connection, specifically to avoid RocksDB lock contention on the same on-disk path.

pages.title: Memory Algorithm
pages.summary: The April-2026 (SDK v2.0.0/v3.0.0) rewrite of mem0's memory pipeline: a single-pass ADD-only extractor (one LLM call, no UPDATE/DELETE, memories accumulate) and a multi-signal hybrid retriever that fuses dense semantic similarity, BM25 keyword matching over lemmatized text, and an entity-linking boost into one combined score. Extraction grounds relative time references to absolute dates so dated instances become independently retrievable, enabling temporal queries. Entity linking (the OSS replacement for graph memory) stores entities in a parallel vector collection and consumes them only as a retrieval boost. spaCy is an optional [nlp] extra; without it the system degrades to semantic-only.

surprises.title: Single LLM call replaces extract-then-diff, no UPDATE/DELETE
surprises.detail: The pre-v3 algorithm used two LLM calls (extract facts, then diff against existing state for ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NONE). The April-2026 algorithm collapses this into one ADD-only call. add() now returns only event:'ADD'; memories accumulate and nothing is overwritten or deleted. Code branching on UPDATE/DELETE events silently never fires.

surprises.title: Anti-hallucination integer ID mapping for dedup context
surprises.detail: Existing memories shown to the LLM for dedup are presented with sequential integer IDs ('0','1',...) while a separate uuid_mapping dict resolves them back to real UUIDs. The model never sees raw UUIDs, so it cannot fabricate or corrupt an identifier. Persisted memories always get a fresh uuid.uuid4().

surprises.title: Adaptive divisor keeps fused scores comparable across stores
surprises.detail: score_and_rank normalizes the additive sum by max_possible, which adapts to which signals fired (1.0 semantic-only, 2.0 +BM25, 2.5 +entity, 1.5 semantic+entity). Threshold gates the semantic score BEFORE combining, so BM25/entity can never resurrect a sub-threshold candidate. Entity/BM25 are additive bonuses, never a re-weighting of baseline semantic relevance.

surprises.title: Entity boost is spread-attenuated to avoid hub domination
surprises.detail: _compute_entity_boosts attenuates an entity's boost quadratically by how many memories it links to: memory_count_weight = 1/(1+0.001*(num_linked-1)^2), boost = similarity * 0.5 * weight. A hyper-connected entity (e.g. the user's own name) thus contributes far less per memory, capped at ENTITY_BOOST_WEIGHT=0.5.

surprises.title: spaCy [nlp] extra is optional; absence silently degrades retrieval
surprises.detail: Without mem0ai[nlp], extract_entities returns [] (no entity linking/boost) and lemmatize_for_bm25 returns raw text. Qdrant additionally needs fastembed for BM25 sparse vectors and logs a warning and disables BM25 if missing. spacy_models.py auto-downloads en_core_web_sm on first use and sets sticky failure flags otherwise.

surprises.title: Cross-language collection breaks BM25
surprises.detail: Python SDK writes the lemmatized field as text_lemmatized (snake_case); the TypeScript SDK writes textLemmatized (camelCase). Sharing one Qdrant collection between SDKs silently breaks lemma-based BM25 matching across languages; collections must be language-scoped.

surprises.title: Temporal reasoning is an extraction-time emergent property
surprises.detail: There is no time-decay ranking function. Relative time references are resolved to absolute dates against the Observation Date inside ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT, and ADD-only means each dated instance is a separate retrievable memory. 'Where did I live before SF?' matches the past instance directly, which is why the benchmark rose from 51% to 93%.

surprises.title: Legacy two-call prompts still ship but are dormant
surprises.detail: prompts.py still defines FACT_RETRIEVAL_PROMPT, USER/AGENT_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT, DEFAULT_UPDATE_MEMORY_PROMPT and get_update_memory_messages, referenced only by memory/utils.py. They are NOT wired into the active _add_to_vector_store path, which uses only ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT. PROCEDURAL_MEMORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT remains live.

pages.title: Configuration System
pages.summary: mem0 is configuration-driven: a single Pydantic v2 MemoryConfig (in mem0/configs/base.py) aggregates four {provider, config} sub-config wrappers for the LLM, embedder, vector store, and optional reranker, plus scalar settings like history_db_path, version, and custom_instructions. Four factories in mem0/utils/factory.py (LlmFactory, EmbedderFactory, VectorStoreFactory, RerankerFactory) map provider strings to implementation class paths and lazily import them via load_class(), turning config dicts into live provider instances. The default stack is OpenAI LLM + embedder + local Qdrant, so a bare Memory() works with just OPENAI_API_KEY. Both nested-dict (Memory.from_config) and typed-object construction converge on the same validated tree.

surprises.title: MemoryConfig has custom_instructions, not custom_fact_extraction_prompt
surprises.detail: The real model in mem0/configs/base.py exposes a single custom_instructions field for fact-extraction guidance. There is no custom_fact_extraction_prompt or custom_update_memory_prompt field on MemoryConfig; custom_update_memory_prompt exists only as a parameter of get_update_memory_messages() in mem0/configs/prompts.py. At add() time a per-call prompt= argument overrides it (custom_instr = prompt or self.custom_instructions).

surprises.title: No graph_store in MemoryConfig — graph memory removed from OSS core
surprises.detail: MemoryConfig has no graph_store field. Graph memory is deprecated/removed; entity linking via a lazily-built per-collection entity store ({collection}_entities) through VectorStoreFactory replaces it.

surprises.title: Asymmetric wrappers: only VectorStoreConfig eagerly types its inner config
surprises.detail: LlmConfig and EmbedderConfig keep their inner config as a raw dict (field_validator only checks the provider name). VectorStoreConfig's @model_validator(mode='after') immediately imports and instantiates the typed provider config class (e.g. QdrantConfig), which is why the engine can read self.config.vector_store.config.collection_name as an attribute while LLM/embedder configs stay dicts until factory time.

surprises.title: BaseLlmConfig->provider config re-projection silently drops reasoning_effort
surprises.detail: In LlmFactory.create, when a BaseLlmConfig object (not a dict) is converted to a provider-specific config, only a fixed list of common attributes is copied (model, temperature, api_key, max_tokens, top_p, top_k, enable_vision, vision_details, http_client_proxies). reasoning_effort is NOT in that list, so passing a base config object can lose it; the dict path is safe because it spreads the whole dict.

surprises.title: EmbedderFactory returns MockEmbeddings for Upstash self-embedding
surprises.detail: EmbedderFactory.create takes a third vector_config argument; when provider is upstash_vector and vector_config.enable_embeddings is true, it returns a no-op MockEmbeddings() instead of a real embedder, because Upstash performs embedding server-side.

surprises.title: Dict vs object configs differ for file-backed vector stores
surprises.detail: VectorStoreConfig's validator injects a default path=/tmp/{provider} only when config is a dict and the provider config class declares a 'path' annotation. If you pass an already-constructed provider-config object, that path injection is skipped — so dict-style and object-style configs are not perfectly interchangeable for file-backed stores.

surprises.title: Lazy SDK imports keep config construction cheap
surprises.detail: Because all provider SDK imports are deferred to load_class() (importlib) at factory time, importing mem0 and building a MemoryConfig is cheap regardless of how many backends are installed; you only pay import cost for providers you actually instantiate.

surprises.title: RerankerFactory points at mem0.reranker.* (singular)
surprises.detail: While reranker config classes live under mem0/configs/rerankers/ (plural), RerankerFactory implementation paths reference the singular mem0.reranker.* package, e.g. mem0.reranker.cohere_reranker.CohereReranker.

pages.title: LLM Providers
pages.summary: The LLM layer is a plugin family where every provider subclasses LLMBase and implements one generate_response method returning a string or a normalised tool-call dict. There are 18 provider implementations spanning OpenAI-compatible APIs, native Anthropic/Gemini/Bedrock SDKs, local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM), and aggregators (LiteLLM, LangChain), wired by LlmFactory. The default is the openai provider on gpt-5-mini. Structured output is handled primarily via response_format JSON mode, with dedicated openai_structured/azure_openai_structured variants for schema-validated parsing.

surprises.title: Abstract signature omits response_format but every provider declares it
surprises.detail: LLMBase.generate_response declares only (messages, tools, tool_choice, **kwargs), yet the engine always calls it with response_format={'type':'json_object'}. Concrete providers add response_format explicitly; SarvamLLM accepts it only to ignore it.

surprises.title: xai and sarvam silently drop tools/tool_choice
surprises.detail: XAILLM and SarvamLLM generate_response signatures have no tool parameters, so any tool-calling caller gets plain text. They still work for memory extraction because the algorithm uses response_format JSON, not tools.

surprises.title: Two *_structured providers, but only one uses the beta parse endpoint
surprises.detail: OpenAIStructuredLLM calls client.beta.chat.completions.parse for schema validation, but AzureOpenAIStructuredLLM still calls chat.completions.create — it is effectively a leaner copy of AzureOpenAILLM, not a true structured-parse path.

surprises.title: AWS Bedrock pings the control plane during construction
surprises.detail: AWSBedrockLLM.__init__ calls list_foundation_models to validate region/model, adding a network round-trip to Memory() setup for Bedrock users (failures downgraded to a warning).

surprises.title: OpenAI store param is opt-in to protect compatible backends
surprises.detail: OpenAILLM only sends 'store' when explicitly configured, because OpenAI-compatible backends (Gemini, Groq, vLLM via the OpenAI client) reject unknown fields.

surprises.title: Anthropic and Bedrock omit top_p when temperature is set
surprises.detail: Both the native AnthropicLLM and AWSBedrockLLM (_build_inference_config) drop top_p/topP when temperature is present, because Anthropic and MiniMax reasoning models raise a ValidationException if both are sent.

surprises.title: extract_json salvages dirty/fenced JSON from weak models
surprises.detail: Tool arguments and JSON bodies pass through mem0.memory.utils.extract_json before json.loads, recovering JSON wrapped in markdown fences or prose — a recurring failure mode for small/local models. Bedrock even round-trips dict input through it.

surprises.title: Lazy string-path imports make SDKs optional
surprises.detail: LlmFactory stores class paths as strings and importlib-loads them on demand; each native-SDK provider wraps its import in try/except ImportError with a pip-install hint, so you only install SDKs for providers you use.

surprises.title: gpt-5-mini default is deliberately NOT treated as a reasoning model
surprises.detail: _is_reasoning_model matches exact gpt-5/gpt-5o names and o1-/o3- prefixes but deliberately excludes gpt-5.x variants like gpt-5.4-mini, which support temperature. The default gpt-5-mini therefore goes through full sampling params.

surprises.title: Azure providers rewrite the word 'assistant' to 'ai' in the last message
surprises.detail: Both AzureOpenAILLM and AzureOpenAIStructuredLLM replace the literal substring 'assistant' with 'ai' in the final user message before sending — an undocumented behavioral quirk that can mangle legitimate content.

pages.title: Embedding Providers
pages.summary: The embeddings layer converts text into dense vectors via a single abstract contract, EmbeddingBase.embed(text, memory_action), implemented by 11 real providers (plus a 10-dim MockEmbeddings for tests) and wired by EmbedderFactory from a declarative EmbedderConfig. It defaults to OpenAI text-embedding-3-small at 1536 dims. A key seam: the embedder's embedding_dims and the vector store's embedding_model_dims are separate, non-auto-synced fields that both default to 1536 — switching to a non-1536 model requires updating the vector store config by hand. Only Vertex AI uses the memory_action argument (mapping add/update/search to RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT/RETRIEVAL_QUERY task types).

surprises.title: Two unsynced dimension fields
surprises.detail: embedder.config.embedding_dims and vector_store.config.embedding_model_dims are independent. Nothing in MemoryConfig copies one into the other; both happen to default to 1536. Choosing a non-1536 model (Gemini 768, Vertex 256, FastEmbed/HF auto-detect) without also setting embedding_model_dims creates a wrong-width index and breaks inserts.

surprises.title: Only Vertex AI uses memory_action
surprises.detail: The engine tags every embed() call with add/search/update, but of 11 providers only VertexAIEmbedding branches on it (RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT vs RETRIEVAL_QUERY vs SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY). The argument is plumbed everywhere as a forward-looking hook; the other 10 providers accept and ignore it.

surprises.title: OpenAI/Azure batch re-sorts by response index
surprises.detail: embed_batch overrides for OpenAI and Azure chunk into batches of 100 and re-sort response.data by .index before returning, because the embeddings API does not guarantee output order matches input order. A naive list comprehension would silently misalign vectors with their source texts.

surprises.title: Ollama can pip-install itself at import
surprises.detail: If the ollama package is missing, the module prompts input('Install it now? [y/N]') and runs pip install via subprocess at import time. In a non-interactive server this blocks on stdin or installs packages at runtime.

surprises.title: Empty package __init__.py enables lazy SDK loading
surprises.detail: mem0/embeddings/__init__.py is 0 bytes; nothing is re-exported. The factory loads each provider by fully-qualified string path via importlib, so importing mem0.embeddings never pulls heavy SDKs (boto3, sentence-transformers, google-genai).

surprises.title: Abstract embed() signature lacks the default every subclass adds
surprises.detail: EmbeddingBase.embed declares memory_action as a required positional with no default, but all 11 concrete providers redeclare it as =None. A custom subclass copying the base signature literally would break call sites that omit the argument.

surprises.title: MockEmbeddings makes all memories identical
surprises.detail: MockEmbeddings.embed always returns the same fixed 10-dim vector, so cosine similarity between any two memories is 1.0 and ranking is meaningless. Fine for plumbing tests, useless for retrieval-quality tests. Also used as the no-op stand-in for Upstash server-side embedding.

surprises.title: OPENAI_API_BASE deprecated
surprises.detail: OpenAIEmbedding emits a DeprecationWarning for the OPENAI_API_BASE env var, slated for removal in 0.1.80; OPENAI_BASE_URL is the replacement.

pages.title: Vector Stores
pages.summary: The vector store layer persists each mem0 memory as a dense embedding plus a flat JSON payload across 24 pluggable backends behind one abstract interface, VectorStoreBase. Stores share an insert/search/get/list/delete/update contract plus collection lifecycle ops, and an enhanced filter dialect (comparison, list, string, and AND/OR/NOT logical operators) that each provider translates natively. Qdrant is the default and richest implementation with hybrid dense + BM25 sparse search; pgvector ships rich SQL filter operators; 15 of 24 providers add native keyword/BM25 search consumed by the hybrid retrieval algorithm.

surprises.title: keyword_search returns None as a sentinel, not []
surprises.detail: VectorStoreBase.keyword_search defaults to returning None to signal 'not supported'. The engine checks `if keyword_results is not None` before fusing BM25 scores, so unsupported stores silently degrade to semantic-only. Returning [] would falsely claim support with zero hits.

surprises.title: No shared result class; results are duck-typed
surprises.detail: There is no single OutputData. ~20 providers each define a local OutputData(BaseModel) with id/score/payload, Redis uses MemoryResult, and Qdrant returns native qdrant_client point objects. The engine reads .id/.score/.payload by attribute.

surprises.title: list() return nesting is inconsistent across stores
surprises.detail: pgvector/turbopuffer/redis return doubly-nested [[OutputData,...]], Qdrant's list() returns the raw scroll() tuple (points, next_offset), while search() returns a flat list. Callers must know which method they called.

surprises.title: pgvector boolean filter casing fix
surprises.detail: PR #5264 serializes boolean filter values with json.dumps (true/false) instead of Python str (True/False) so they match JSONB storage. Same PR added LIKE wildcard escaping (\, %, _ + ESCAPE) and TS scalar coercion; earlier #4997 closed SQL injection via psycopg.sql.Identifier and bound params.

surprises.title: Score sign/scale is not normalized across stores
surprises.detail: pgvector returns cosine distance (lower=closer), turbopuffer returns 1 - dist, Redis returns raw vector_distance. Raw .score values are not comparable across backends; the engine's fusion accounts for this.

surprises.title: Qdrant pre-v3 collections cannot do BM25
surprises.detail: Collections created before hybrid search lack the named 'bm25' sparse slot; writing into them is rejected ('Not existing vector name error: bm25'). Qdrant detects this via _has_bm25_slot on init, warns, and disables BM25 (semantic still works). fastembed is optional and lazy-loaded.

surprises.title: FAISS filters via in-memory post-filtering
surprises.detail: FAISS has no server-side filter engine: it over-fetches (fetch_k = top_k*2) then runs _apply_filters in Python, so filtered searches can under-return when matches fall outside the over-fetch window.

surprises.title: Only Qdrant overrides search_batch
surprises.detail: The base search_batch loops over search() sequentially. Qdrant is the sole store with a native batched implementation (query_batch_points) plus a sequential fallback on error.

surprises.title: text_lemmatized is precomputed at write time
surprises.detail: The engine writes a lemmatized copy of the memory text into the payload at insert, so keyword/BM25 search only lemmatizes the query at read time rather than re-tokenizing the corpus, keeping hybrid search cheap enough to run on every search().

pages.title: Rerankers
pages.summary: The reranker layer is an optional, opt-in second-stage scorer that re-orders candidate memories returned by mem0's multi-signal retrieval before they are returned to the caller. Every provider subclasses BaseReranker and implements a single rerank(query, documents, top_k) method that attaches a rerank_score and returns documents sorted descending. Five providers ship (cohere, sentence_transformer, huggingface, llm_reranker, zero_entropy) spanning hosted APIs, local cross-encoders, and LLM-as-judge. Reranking runs only when a reranker is configured in MemoryConfig.reranker AND the caller passes rerank=True to search().

surprises.title: Two independent guards gate reranking
surprises.detail: Reranking runs only if BOTH a reranker is configured (MemoryConfig.reranker non-None) AND search(rerank=True) is passed. Either alone is a silent no-op, and an empty result set also short-circuits it (and original_memories).

surprises.title: Silent provider-level fallback to rerank_score 0.0
surprises.detail: Every provider wraps scoring in bare except Exception and falls back to the original order with rerank_score=0.0 (LLMReranker uses 0.5 per-document). Failures are silent; uniform 0.0 scores mean reranking failed and you are seeing unreranked order.

surprises.title: rerank_score scales are not comparable across providers
surprises.detail: Cohere/ZeroEntropy return API relevance scores, LLMReranker returns 0.0-1.0 judged scores, SentenceTransformer returns raw unbounded cross-encoder logits, HuggingFace optionally min-max normalises to [0,1]. No common scale.

surprises.title: LLMReranker makes N LLM calls per search
surprises.detail: It scores each candidate document with a separate synchronous LLM call, making it by far the slowest/most expensive provider; best for small pools or offline eval.

surprises.title: LLMReranker prompt-injection hardening
surprises.detail: Truncates query and document to _MAX_INPUT_LEN=4000 chars and sends instructions as a system message with user data in the user role so memory text cannot override scoring instructions.

surprises.title: scoring_prompt is deprecated on LLMRerankerConfig
surprises.detail: If supplied, it is now used as the system message and emits a DeprecationWarning; the built-in banded rubric prompt is preferred.

surprises.title: __init__.py export set is incomplete
surprises.detail: mem0/reranker/__init__.py only re-exports BaseReranker, CohereReranker, SentenceTransformerReranker. The other three providers work via the factory's lazy dotted-path import but are absent from __all__, so count the *_reranker.py files (five) for the true set.

surprises.title: Provider keys differ from class/file names
surprises.detail: Factory keys are llm_reranker (not llm) and sentence_transformer (singular). A wrong key raises ValueError: Unsupported reranker provider.

surprises.title: Cohere trusts API order, ZeroEntropy re-sorts client-side
surprises.detail: CohereReranker relies on the API's returned order and top_n, while ZeroEntropyReranker explicitly re-sorts the results descending and applies top_k itself despite calling a similar rerank API.

pages.title: Graph Memory (deprecated)
pages.summary: Graph Memory was an optional relationship-aware retrieval layer that layered a property graph (Neo4j, Memgraph, Kuzu, Apache AGE, Amazon Neptune) over mem0's vector store, opted into via a graph_store section of MemoryConfig and an enable_graph flag. It has been removed entirely from both the Python and TypeScript OSS packages in the v3 rewrite (commit 59880a6f), with docs cleaned up in #5277. Its function — surfacing memories connected through shared entities — is now handled by native entity linking: a sibling {collection}_entities vector collection plus a retrieval-time entity boost (ENTITY_BOOST_WEIGHT=0.5) fused into the combined score, requiring no external graph database. Users upgrading should drop enable_graph/graph_store config; no data migration is needed, but the old relations field is no longer populated.

surprises.title: Graph memory is removed, not just deprecated
surprises.detail: There is no mem0/graphs/ directory, no graph_memory.py/memgraph_memory.py/kuzu_memory.py, no graph references in mem0/memory/main.py, and no mem0-ts/src/oss/src/graphs/. The enable_graph/graph_store and enableGraph/graphStore config keys are silently ignored, not honored. Finalized in commit 59880a6f.

surprises.title: Cypher sanitization helpers survive as dead code
surprises.detail: sanitize_relationship_for_cypher() and remove_spaces_from_entities() still live in mem0/memory/utils.py and are tested by tests/memory/test_memory_utils.py with Neo4j/Memgraph/Kuzu/Neptune docstrings, but remove_spaces_from_entities has no non-test caller anywhere in mem0/ — it is vestigial.

surprises.title: 'Entity graph' naming is conceptual, not a graph DB
surprises.detail: The migration guide and mem0/configs/prompts.py still say 'entity graph boost' and 'build a graph of related memories,' but there is no graph database or traversal — it refers to memory-to-memory links in payload fields scored at retrieval time.

surprises.title: Neptune survives as a vector store, not a graph store
surprises.detail: mem0/vector_stores/neptune_analytics.py remains as a vector index provider, distinct from the removed Neptune graph adapters that lived under mem0/graphs/neptune/. Same vendor, different feature.

surprises.title: The relations field is a silent breaking change
surprises.detail: search()/get_all() no longer populate the old relations key. Entity relationships are consumed only through retrieval ranking and are not exposed as a queryable graph; apps that traversed triples directly must be redesigned with no drop-in equivalent.

surprises.title: Graph memory doubled LLM cost when enabled
surprises.detail: A configured graph store ran a second LLM extraction pass per add() to mint triples and used a ThreadPoolExecutor fan-out (commit a6130c54 added a skip-when-disabled fast path). V3 entity extraction uses local spaCy NLP with zero LLM calls.

surprises.title: Entity store reuses the same vector provider
surprises.detail: Memory.entity_store lazily creates a {collection_name}_entities collection via the same VectorStoreFactory provider; for Qdrant embedded mode it reuses the existing client to avoid RocksDB lock contention. No separate database is configured.

pages.title: Hosted Client & Proxy
pages.summary: Documents the hosted-platform clients MemoryClient (sync) and AsyncMemoryClient (async) in mem0/client/main.py — thin httpx wrappers over api.mem0.ai authenticated by MEM0_API_KEY, with org_id/project_id resolved from the key via GET /v1/ping/. Covers every public method (add/search/get/get_all/update/delete/delete_all/history/users/delete_users/reset/batch_update/batch_delete/export/summary/feedback/webhooks), the typed Pydantic option models, the api_error_handler decorator that maps HTTP status codes to structured MemoryError subclasses, telemetry capture, the Project/AsyncProject management API, and the LiteLLM-based chat-completion proxy that retrieves+injects memories and writes new turns on a daemon thread. Contrasts the HTTP client with the in-process self-hosted engine and notes the recent delete_linked and latest_only/latestOnly features on hosted reads.

surprises.title: Async client validates its API key with blocking requests in __init__
surprises.detail: AsyncMemoryClient._validate_api_key() uses the synchronous requests library and is called directly inside __init__, so constructing the async client performs one blocking network round-trip before any await; only later memory operations use the non-blocking httpx.AsyncClient.

surprises.title: Entity-param guard is asymmetric across methods
surprises.detail: search() and get_all() reject top-level user_id/agent_id/app_id/run_id (ENTITY_PARAMS) and force them into filters={...}, but add() and delete_all() accept the same kwargs at top level — so identity params are valid on writes yet rejected on reads.

surprises.title: Importing the proxy can trigger a live pip install
surprises.detail: mem0/proxy/main.py runs import litellm at module load and, if missing, shells out to pip install litellm in a subprocess (exiting the process on failure) — a surprising import-time side effect in locked-down environments.

surprises.title: Proxy writes memories fire-and-forget on a daemon thread
surprises.detail: Completions._async_add_to_memory spawns a daemon thread calling mem0_client.add(...), so a slow/failed write never blocks or breaks the chat response, but failures are silent and a memory written this turn is not guaranteed searchable on the immediate next turn.

surprises.title: org_id/project_id resolved from key, never injected into memory params
surprises.detail: MemoryClient._prepare_params intentionally omits org_id/project_id (resolved server-side from the API key via /v1/ping/), while only the Project manager injects them into the URL/query for org/project-scoped endpoints.

surprises.title: Endpoint paths straddle v1/v2/v3 API generations
surprises.detail: Memory add/read/search use /v3/, per-ID ops + history + batch + exports + feedback + entity listing use /v1/, entity deletion uses /v2/entities/, and project/webhook management uses /api/v1/ — and the option-model docstrings still say 'v2 API' for search/get_all despite the code posting to v3.

surprises.title: get_project/update_project deprecated in favor of client.project
surprises.detail: MemoryClient.get_project()/update_project() log a deprecation warning steering callers to client.project.get()/update() and are slated for removal in package v1.0; the surfaces are not perfectly aligned (memory_depth/usecase_setting exist only on the legacy methods).

surprises.title: delete_linked is the delete-side counterpart of latest_only
surprises.detail: delete(memory_id, delete_linked=True) transitively removes the older memories a memory superseded (the v3 linked_memory_ids chain) so a superseded memory cannot resurface; the flag is normalized via {'delete_linked': delete_linked or None} so it is omitted when False.

pages.title: Self-Hosted Server
pages.summary: The server/ directory is a standalone FastAPI app that wraps the OSS Memory engine in a secure REST API plus a Next.js dashboard. Auth is on by default (Bearer JWT, per-user X-API-Key, or legacy ADMIN_API_KEY), the server refuses to boot without JWT_SECRET unless AUTH_DISABLED=true, and state lives in two Postgres databases on one pgvector instance (memories + a mem0_app auth/audit DB migrated by Alembic). Notable mechanics include single-use rotating refresh tokens, constant-time login, slowapi rate limits on auth routes, off-hot-path request logging with BRIN-indexed pruning, an upstream-error classifier returning clean 502s, and the recent /search 502 fix with rich pgvector filter operators.

surprises.title: No Neo4j/APOC in the self-hosted stack
surprises.detail: Despite common assumptions, server/docker-compose.yaml defines only three services: mem0 (API), postgres (ankane/pgvector:v0.5.1), and mem0-dashboard. There is no Neo4j/APOC container. The graph DB stack only appears via the dev.Dockerfile installing mem0ai[graph]; graph memory is deprecated in OSS core.

surprises.title: At-most-one admin enforced at the DB layer
surprises.detail: Migration 004_unique_admin_role.py adds a partial unique index on users(role) WHERE role='admin'. Combined with register()'s 'registration is closed once any user exists' guard and its IntegrityError rollback, the first registrant becomes the sole admin and the endpoint locks shut.

surprises.title: Single-use refresh tokens via conditional UPDATE
surprises.detail: consume_refresh_jti() uses UPDATE refresh_token_jtis SET used_at=now WHERE jti=? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at>now, then checks rowcount==0 to 401. This closes the read-check-write race so concurrent token replays race on a single row and at most one wins.

surprises.title: Constant-time login to avoid email enumeration
surprises.detail: login() calls dummy_verify_password() (pwd_context.dummy_verify) when the email is not found, burning the same bcrypt cycles as a real verify so response timing does not leak whether an account exists.

surprises.title: Request logs are written off the hot path and pruned manually
surprises.detail: _persist_request_log runs via loop.run_in_executor so DB writes never block responses. The append-only request_logs table (~864k rows/day at 10 req/s) uses a BRIN index on created_at (migration 006) and is pruned only by scripts/prune_request_logs.py / make prune-logs — nothing prunes automatically.

surprises.title: /search 502 fix folded deprecated top-level identifiers into filters
surprises.detail: PR #5263 stopped splatting the whole SearchRequest into Memory.search(); top-level user_id/agent_id/run_id (now deprecated) are merged into the filters dict and only top_k/threshold are forwarded, fixing a 502 when identifiers were passed alongside filters.

surprises.title: SQL-injection-safe rich pgvector filter operators
surprises.detail: OPERATOR_SQL_MAP + _build_filter_conditions compile eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/in/nin/contains/icontains plus $or/$not and a '*' key-exists sentinel into parameterised SQL over the JSONB payload. contains/icontains escape backslash/%/underscore and add ESCAPE '\'; a follow-up (#5264) fixed boolean casing via json.dumps.

surprises.title: Upstream errors are classified by walking the exception chain
surprises.detail: errors.py _classify walks __cause__/__context__ so wrapped provider errors still map to stable codes (provider_auth_failed, provider_rate_limited, datastore_unavailable, vector_store_unavailable, etc.), returning HTTP 502 with a request_id and no stack trace.

surprises.title: Runtime config persists to DB and layers over .env
surprises.detail: server_state.py keeps a single process-global Memory instance behind an RLock; POST /configure deep-merges and upserts overrides into the settings table (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE). On restart, persisted overrides re-apply on top of .env-derived defaults.

surprises.detail: BUNDLED_LLM_PROVIDERS=(openai,anthropic,gemini) and BUNDLED_EMBEDDER_PROVIDERS=(openai,gemini); _validate_bundled_providers returns 400 if a config selects a provider whose package isn't in the image.

pages.title: TypeScript SDK
pages.summary: The mem0ai npm package (mem0-ts/) ships two surfaces: a thin hosted-platform client (import { MemoryClient } from "mem0ai") and a self-contained OSS memory engine (import { Memory } from "mem0ai/oss"). The OSS side is a faithful port of the Python Memory engine — same config-driven provider factories, same April-2026 single-pass additive extraction algorithm, same entity-linking retrieval — built dual-format (CJS+ESM) with tsup and tested with Jest. Key divergences from Python: no AsyncMemory/AsyncMemoryClient duplicate classes (everything is already promise-based), no LLM proxy wrapper, no graph-memory store and no OSS reranker layer; the TS provider roster is a curated subset (11 LLMs, 6 embedders, 8 vector stores).

surprises.title: No AsyncMemory or AsyncMemoryClient in TypeScript
surprises.detail: Python duplicates every engine/client method into sync and async classes. The TS SDK has exactly one Memory class and one MemoryClient because all methods already return Promises — a structural divergence, not a feature gap.

surprises.title: OSS README is stale and misleading
surprises.detail: src/oss/README.md still shows import { Memory } from "mem0-ts" (wrong package name; real is mem0ai/oss), a legacy positional add("text","user123") signature, and advertises 'Optional graph-based memory relationships' — none of which match the code. The package is named mem0ai and uses an entity store, not a graph DB.

surprises.title: No graph database in the OSS TS engine
surprises.detail: There is no graphs/ subdir, no Neo4j/Memgraph provider, and no graph factory. Relationship awareness comes from a lazily-created <collection>_entities vector collection plus compromise-based NLP entity extraction. The only 'graph' mentions are a prompt example and a test name.

surprises.title: latestOnly and deleteLinked are wired on the hosted client
surprises.detail: latestOnly?: boolean (search/getAll) serializes to latest_only via camelToSnakeKeys; deleteLinked?: boolean (delete) is off by default and serializes to the delete_linked query param, cascading deletion of superseded v3 linked-chain memories. Both verified by jest tests.

surprises.title: Filter normalization prevents 'undefined' wire footguns
surprises.detail: search()/getAll() drop entity-id keys that resolve to undefined because Qdrant rejects the malformed match, pgvector binds NULL, and Redis emits a literal 'undefined' string in TAG filters. Top-level entity params throw via rejectTopLevelEntityParams().

surprises.title: Self-healing deferred initialization
surprises.detail: Vector-store creation is deferred to _autoInitialize() (so embedding dimension can be auto-probed). _ensureInitialized() stores the first failure instead of throwing from the constructor and retries on the next method call, surviving a transiently-down embedder/store at startup.

surprises.title: All heavy deps are external peer dependencies
surprises.detail: tsup marks every provider client (OpenAI, Anthropic, pg, redis, qdrant, supabase, azure, cloudflare, langchain, better-sqlite3, compromise, natural) as external; providers import them lazily and a tsup-externals.test.ts guards it, so a minimal install pulls nothing extra.

surprises.title: compromise NLP is optional with regex fallback

pages.title: OpenMemory Platform
pages.summary: OpenMemory is a self-hosted, single-user memory platform under openmemory/ that wraps the mem0 OSS Memory engine in a FastAPI service, exposes five memory tools over an MCP server (port 8765, SSE + Streamable HTTP transports), and ships a Next.js 15 / React 19 dashboard (port 3000) backed by Redux Toolkit. It keeps a relational SQLite mirror (state, ACLs, audit logs, categories) alongside vectors stored in Qdrant by default (port 6333), with provider auto-detection and a three-revision Alembic chain. It is operationally distinct from server/: no auth, open CORS, one implicit user, intended for local use.

surprises.title: create_all and Alembic both own the schema
surprises.detail: main.py calls Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) at import, so fresh installs build the schema from ORM models, while the Alembic chain is a separate, manually-run mechanism (make migrate). A model change not also encoded as a migration appears on new installs but never on upgraded ones.

surprises.title: PUT /api/v1/config/ silently discards the update
surprises.detail: update_configuration() in routers/config.py builds updated_config but never calls save_config_to_db() and returns None implicitly. The working paths are PATCH / and the granular /mem0/llm, /mem0/embedder, /mem0/vector_store, /openmemory setters (which the dashboard uses).

surprises.title: MCP search bypasses the engine retrieval pipeline
surprises.detail: search_memory does not call memory_client.search(); it manually embeds the query and calls vector_store.search() with limit=10, sidestepping reranking/score-fusion/entity-linking. MCP search returns raw vector hits, not the engine's fused ranking.

surprises.title: Auto-categorization is hard-wired to OpenAI
surprises.detail: categorization.py instantiates a bare OpenAI() client and always calls gpt-4o-mini regardless of the configured LLM provider, so categorization needs OPENAI_API_KEY even on Ollama/Anthropic setups. It runs inside SQLAlchemy after_insert/after_update event listeners via a separate Session.

surprises.title: Migration Create Date is misleading
surprises.detail: add_config_table carries Create Date 2023-06-01 yet its down_revision is the 2025 initial migration. The chain order is defined solely by down_revision, never the docstring timestamp; editing an applied migration desyncs alembic_version across databases.

surprises.title: No auth, open CORS, spoofable MCP identity
surprises.detail: allow_origins=['*'], no API keys, a single implicit user, and MCP identity carried only in the URL path (/mcp/{client_name}/.../{user_id}). Acceptable for a localhost single-user tool, unsafe for shared/networked hosting — use server/ for that.

surprises.title: Resilient lazy memory-client init
surprises.detail: get_memory_client_safe() returns None on failure and every MCP tool degrades to a 'Memory system unavailable' string instead of crashing, keeping the MCP server alive when the LLM/embedder (e.g. Ollama) is down.

surprises.title: UI env vars are sed-replaced into a prebuilt bundle
surprises.detail: ui/Dockerfile builds Next.js with placeholder NEXT_PUBLIC_* strings; entrypoint.sh sed-replaces them in .next/ at container start, so one prebuilt image is re-pointed at a new API URL/user without rebuilding — but requires a restart, not a reload.

pages.title: Integrations & Ecosystem
pages.summary: Surveys mem0's first-party clients and editor plugins: the Python (mem0-cli) and Node (@mem0/cli) CLIs with their Agent Mode <5s key bootstrap and AGENTRUSH game; the mem0-plugin that wires Claude Code/Cursor/Codex/OpenCode/Antigravity to the remote MCP server (mcp.mem0.ai) with lifecycle hooks for automatic capture and nine MCP tools; the @mem0/openclaw-mem0 plugin with token-budgeted recall, pre-extraction filtering, per-agent isolation, and the cost-gated dream consolidation; the @mem0/vercel-ai-provider for AI SDK v5; and the reference vs pipeline skills. Each integration's package, install, and connection path (REST, MCP, or embedded mem0ai SDK) is documented against the source.

surprises.title: The CLI [oss] extra is declared but unwired
surprises.detail: cli/python/pyproject.toml declares oss = ["mem0ai>=0.1.0"] and the README/help advertise --graph flags, but backend/base.py get_backend() unconditionally returns PlatformBackend — there is no OssBackend in the backend package, and --graph/--no-graph appear only in the static _build_help_json() dict, not on the live add/search commands.

surprises.title: --agent is overloaded with two meanings
surprises.detail: As a global flag --agent toggles JSON-envelope output; but mem0 init --agent is a subcommand flag that bootstraps an Agent Mode account. main() special-cases this in argv: when init is present it leaves --agent in place and only strips --json as the output toggle.

surprises.title: Env-var detection triggers Agent Mode but never names the agent
surprises.detail: agent_detect.detect_agent_caller() recognises CLAUDECODE/CURSOR_AGENT/CODEX_CLI etc. only as a context trigger to enable auto-bootstrap; the canonical agent_caller identity is self-declared via --agent-caller or mem0 identify and is never sniffed from env vars (Proof-Editor style honesty).

surprises.title: OTP claim upgrades the agent key in place
surprises.detail: claim_via_otp() reuses the email-code flow but adds agent_mode_api_key to the verify body; the backend upgrades the key in place so the API key value never changes, memories transfer, and agent_mode flips false without disrupting a running agent.

surprises.title: Dream-gate orders checks cheapest-first to avoid API calls
surprises.detail: openclaw dream-gate.ts runs two local file-read gates (>=24h since last run AND >=5 sessions) before the one network round-trip for the >=20 memory-count gate, and uses an exclusive wx lock file (reclaimed after 1h) so racing processes can't double-run consolidation.

surprises.title: Plugin hooks are engineered to never block the editor
surprises.detail: Every mem0-plugin hook command ends with 2>/dev/null || true, scripts exit 0 with 3-8s timeouts, and auto_capture.py reads only the transcript tail (200 lines/8000 chars) posting with infer=True so extraction is async — a slow capture can never stall the session.

surprises.title: AGENTRUSH memories are public
surprises.detail: mem0 agent-rush add memories are visible to any other player; the CLI gates the first interactive add on an explicit y confirmation (persisted as agent_rush.acknowledged_at) and for non-TTY agent runs prints the PII warning to stderr and proceeds since agents can't answer y/N.

surprises.title: plugin_sync only edits existing entries, never creates them
surprises.detail: sync_api_key() propagates a new key into ~/.claude/settings.json env and existing export MEM0_API_KEY shell lines via atomic tmp+rename writes, but deliberately never creates new entries or touches Codex/Cursor MCP configs — solving the stale-env-key surprise without clobbering unrelated config.

pages.title: Evaluation & Benchmarks
pages.summary: mem0's benchmarking harness under evaluation/ has two phases: a per-technique experiment runner (run_experiments.py) that drives the hosted mem0 platform plus RAG, full-context, LangMem, Zep, and OpenAI baselines against the LoCoMo dataset, and a scorer (evals.py + generate_scores.py) applying BLEU, token-F1, and a GPT-4o-mini LLM-as-judge. The headline April-2026 results (LoCoMo 91.6, LongMemEval 94.8, BEAM 64.1/48.6 at ~7K tokens and ~1s p50) come from a separate open-sourced framework (mem0ai/memory-benchmarks) and reflect single-pass retrieval with no agentic loops. The in-repo harness only covers LoCoMo; LongMemEval and BEAM runners are not vendored here.

surprises.title: In-repo harness only covers LoCoMo
surprises.detail: run_experiments.py hard-codes dataset/locomo10.json / locomo10_rag.json for every technique. The headline LongMemEval (94.8) and BEAM (64.1/48.6) numbers come from the external github.com/mem0ai/memory-benchmarks repo, not this evaluation/ tree.

surprises.title: Category 5 is silently dropped from scoring
surprises.detail: Both evals.py and metrics/llm_judge.py explicitly `continue` when category == 5 (LoCoMo's adversarial/unanswerable class), so reported accuracy excludes those questions even though the runner still records adversarial_answer fields.

surprises.title: store_true flags ignore their argument
surprises.detail: --filter_memories and --is_graph are argparse store_true flags. Passing `--filter_memories False` still evaluates to True; the README's 'False' default is the absence-of-flag default, not a passable value.

surprises.title: LLM judge is the real headline metric, BLEU/F1 are secondary
surprises.detail: LoCoMo gold answers are terse and generated answers are verbose, so surface-overlap metrics under-report. The generous GPT-4o-mini judge (CORRECT->1) at temperature 0 is what the 91.6/94.8 numbers actually measure.

surprises.title: chunk_size == -1 is the full-context sentinel
surprises.detail: RAGManager.create_chunks short-circuits on chunk_size=-1 to return the whole transcript as one chunk with no embeddings and zero search time, reusing the RAG code path to implement the full-context baseline.

surprises.title: LangMem error path raises UnboundLocalError
surprises.detail: LangMem.search_memory's except block returns `t2 - t1` but t2 is only assigned in the try block before the failing call, so the error handler itself crashes.

surprises.title: Role-swapped ingestion per speaker
surprises.detail: MemoryADD adds the same conversation twice with user/assistant roles swapped (messages vs messages_reverse) so each of the two speakers gets a first-person memory store; the answer prompt explicitly warns the LLM not to confuse character names with memory owners.

surprises.title: Heavy import side effects in metrics/utils.py
surprises.detail: Importing the metrics module downloads NLTK punkt/wordnet and eagerly loads the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 SentenceTransformer at import time, even though the standard scorer only uses BLEU-1 and token-F1.

surprises.title: OpenAI baseline reads pre-dumped files, no live API
surprises.detail: OpenAIPredict reads memories/{idx}.txt exported out-of-band from ChatGPT's memory feature and returns a hard-coded search time of 0; there is no live OpenAI memory API call in the code path.

surprises.title: Zep ingestion gated to first conversation
surprises.detail: ZepAdd.process_all_conversations only ingests when idx == 0, processing a single LoCoMo conversation (likely to control Zep API cost).
